open_points.subject: OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS subject-kind mapping
open_points.text:
which audit action M09 has each accepted owner action write (R0-58) (owner,
2026-11-24).
open_points.question: Does data_provider own both the audit action and AuditSubjectKind selected for every OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS row, or does another module derive the subject kind independently?
options: data_provider owns both values in each OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS row
operations derives AuditSubjectKind from the action or constructed subject
the audit subject model derives its own kind
open_points.default_guess: data_provider owns both the audit action and subject kind in OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS

witness.initial: An owner grants project P to agent session S, so the audit subject must have the session_project form.
events: data_provider supplies the OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS row for the grant
operations constructs and stores the audit entry
outcomes: operations trusts the row's AuditSubjectKind and stores session_project
operations derives the kind independently from the action or subject and may ignore a different value in the row
witness.observer: the audit-log reader or a consistency check of the stored subject discriminator

open_points.subject: new data_provider constants versus its eight typed tables
open_points.text: Its other constants are scalars and import nothing.
open_points.question: Are the newly exported plural constants scalar encodings, collections of primitive values, or typed tables/sets that directly name models or enum members, and which model imports does each require?
options: all are scalar encodings and import nothing
they are primitive collections that import no models
some are typed collections or tables and require additional model or enum imports
open_points.default_guess: treat the plural policy constants as immutable typed collections and declare every model or enum they directly name

witness.initial: The generator builds data_provider with PROJECT_VALUE_FAILURE_KINDS and OWNER_CHANGE_ACTIONS exported.
events: one implementer follows the statement that every non-table constant is scalar
another implementer follows the plural names and represents them as typed sets of enum members
outcomes: the constants contain scalar encoded text and data_provider imports no additional models
the constants contain enum members and data_provider requires additional model imports
witness.observer: the strict import projector and every consumer comparing a value with a member of these constants

open_points.subject: given_values numeric and version readers
open_points.text:
Reading the text forms a value is written in, wherever Registry reads one
(owner, 2026-11-26): an instant, a calendar date, a decimal number, a whole
number, a version's digits and a listener's address (A17 rule 1).
open_points.question: Which exported capability reads a decimal number, which reads a whole number, and whether read_digits_text reads version digits only or also whole-number text?
options: add separate read_decimal_text, read_whole_number_text and read_version_digits_text capabilities
use check_value_forms for decimal and whole numbers and read_digits_text only for versions
use one read_digits_text capability for whole numbers and versions, with another named capability for decimals
open_points.default_guess: add separate readers for decimal text, whole-number text and version digits

open_points.subject: OWNER_FORM_PATH_SEPARATOR
open_points.question: What literal value does this constant hold, what owner-form names it separates, and which module interprets paths built with it?
options: a delimiter interpreted by the owner-interface transport
a delimiter interpreted by given_values
a presentation-only character with no parsing semantics
open_points.default_guess: define one literal delimiter and make the owner-interface form parser its sole interpreter

open_points.subject: text representation constants
open_points.question: What exact encoding name and replacement character are fixed, and in which decoding or encoding operations is replacement permitted instead of refusal?
options: UTF-8 with U+FFFD replacement wherever decoding fails
UTF-8 with replacement only for diagnostics or display
UTF-8 with malformed input refused and the replacement character used only for rendering
open_points.default_guess: use UTF-8, refuse malformed protocol or stored input, and reserve U+FFFD for explicitly defined display replacement

open_points.subject: service wire constants
open_points.text:
CONTENT_TYPE_HEADER
CONTENT_LENGTH_HEADER
SERVICE_AUTHORIZATION_HEADER
SERVICE_AUTHORIZATION_SCHEME
SERVICE_ANSWER_CONTENT_TYPE
SERVICE_INSTANT_UTC_MARK
open_points.question: What exact wire spellings and values do these constants hold, including header-name casing, authorization syntax, answer media type and accepted/rendered UTC marker?
options: standard HTTP spellings with a Bearer-style authorization scheme, a fixed JSON media type and Z for UTC
custom Registry spellings and scheme
case-insensitive parsing with one canonical emitted spelling
open_points.default_guess: accept HTTP header names case-insensitively, emit canonical standard spellings, and define one exact scheme, media type and UTC marker in the service contract

open_points.subject: owner HTTP response constants
open_points.question: What exact header names and form media type do these constants hold, and does the content-security-policy constant name a header or its complete policy value?
options: constants are header names only and the policy value is defined elsewhere
the CSP constant contains the complete header value while the cookie constants name headers
each constant contains the complete emitted field or media-type value
open_points.default_guess: use canonical header names, application/x-www-form-urlencoded for ordinary forms, and define the complete CSP value separately from its header name

open_points.subject: multipart upload constants
open_points.question: What exact multipart grammar do these constants define, including media type, parameter names, delimiter bytes and closing suffix, and which module owns parsing that grammar?
options: standard multipart/form-data grammar parsed by the owner-interface transport
a restricted Registry-specific multipart grammar
library-defined parsing with these constants used only for tests
open_points.default_guess: define a restricted standards-compatible multipart/form-data grammar owned by the owner-interface transport

open_points.subject: backup key digest serialization
open_points.question: What digest algorithm and exact serialized prefix/separator form identify a backup key, and is the same DIGEST_ALGORITHM also used for uploaded-file and content digests?
options: one algorithm and serialization shared by all Registry digests
one algorithm constant with domain-separated serialization for each digest kind
these constants apply only to backup-key digests and other digests have separate definitions
open_points.default_guess: use one explicitly named cryptographic algorithm with domain-separated, kind-specific serialization

open_points.subject: failure-kind policy sets
open_points.question: Which exact refusal or failure members belong to each collection, whether their order is observable, and which module is authoritative for that classification?
options: unordered sets derived from the closed refusal vocabulary
ordered tuples defining diagnostic order
tables mapping each operation to its applicable failure kinds
open_points.default_guess: define ordered immutable collections because failures within one stage are returned together and their output must be deterministic

open_points.subject: runtime-settings metadata
open_points.question: Which exact setting identifiers and order these constants contain, how owner-only startup changes required membership, and whether configuration or runtime_settings owns the grouping semantics?
options: data_provider owns exact ordered identifiers and configuration applies them
runtime_settings owns membership while data_provider only stores names
configuration derives all groups directly from fields and these constants are redundant
open_points.default_guess: data_provider owns the exact ordered identifiers and groups, runtime_settings reads only those identifiers, and configuration applies their startup semantics

open_points.subject: store companion files
open_points.question: Which file suffixes are store companions, what operations may create or remove them, and whether they participate in path separation, startup cleanup and backup snapshots?
options: SQLite journal/WAL/shared-memory suffixes fixed by the selected store mode
only Registry's temporary-store suffix
all files the backend may place beside the store
open_points.default_guess: list exactly the companion files possible under the release-fixed SQLite mode and state their cleanup and backup treatment

open_points.subject: change classification constants
open_points.question: Which exact owner actions and service operations count as changes, and is this classification authoritative for CSRF, HTTP method, transaction, audit and manifest behavior or only one of those concerns?
options: one authoritative change classification reused by every listed concern
separate owner and service classifications used only by transport routing
derived sets copied from OWNER_ACTIONS and the operation table
open_points.default_guess: make these derived, validated views of the authoritative owner-action and operation tables and state every behavior that consumes them

open_points.subject: request-id printability categories
open_points.question: Which Unicode general categories make a request-id character unprintable, and is printability fixed by this closed collection or delegated to a language/library predicate?
options: an explicit closed list of Unicode general categories
the runtime language's isprintable predicate
ASCII printable characters only
open_points.default_guess: define an explicit closed list of Unicode categories so behavior cannot move with the runtime or Unicode library
